title: STEM-CAM: Segmented Thermometer-Encoded Multibit CAM with Wildcard Matching for Efficient Arbitrary-Order Minkowski Distance Metrics
evidence_span: STEM-CAM uses segmented thermometer encoding with wildcard matching to support arbitrary-order Minkowski distance metrics in a multibit CAM; a FeFET-based encoding-aware cell supplies the implementation path and the official description reports high throughput and area/energy efficiency without numeric values.
problem: Conventional digital distance computation and existing CAM designs provide limited parallelism or mainly support L0/L1 metrics, limiting scalable configurable distance-based AI.
method_or_artifact: Segmented thermometer-encoded multibit CAM with wildcard-augmented encoding and an encoding-aware FeFET cell for arbitrary-order Lp metrics.
workload_or_benchmark: Distance-based AI using arbitrary-order Minkowski metrics; exact datasets, dimensions, and evaluation protocol are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: FeFET-based multibit CAM and in-memory distance computation; cell, array, voltage, frequency, and process conditions are unspecified.
baselines: existing CAM designs mainly supporting L0/L1 metrics
metrics: High throughput and area/energy efficiency are reported qualitatively; numeric values are not provided in the official description.
limits: The description provides no numeric throughput, energy, area, accuracy, array-size, or process results.
Metric order, data precision, FeFET operating conditions, and comparison normalization require full-paper review.
Official description only; no independent reproduction.

title: ARTEMIS: Adaptive RL Test-Time Ensemble for Model Inference in SSD Testing
evidence_span: ARTEMIS formulates SSD test-case generation as reinforcement learning, deploys across heterogeneous commercial devices without device-specific customization, and ensembles policies learned under diverse workload distributions for non-stationary environments; it reports more frequent discovery of high-impact blocking garbage-collection events on Meta and User Garbage Collection stress tasks without numeric rates.
problem: Rule-based verification does not scale to complex SSD controllers or changing commercial-device operating environments.
method_or_artifact: Reinforcement-learning test-case generation with test-time policy ensembling across workload distributions and device-agnostic deployment.
workload_or_benchmark: Commercial SSD testing with Meta Garbage Collection and User Garbage Collection stress tasks; device models, traces, test budgets, and event definitions are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Heterogeneous commercial SSD controllers accessed directly by the tester; firmware versions, host platform, NAND configuration, and test duration are unspecified.
metrics: More frequent discovery of critical blocking garbage-collection events is reported qualitatively; event rates, confidence intervals, and test budgets are not provided.
limits: The official description does not provide event counts, test budgets, coverage, false-positive rates, or policy-training details.
Commercial-device diversity and transfer conditions are not exposed.
Official description only; no independent reproduction.

title: Noisexplore: A Device-Aware Hierarchical Noise Modeling and DTCO Framework for Analog In-Pixel Computing Architectures
evidence_span: NoiseXplore integrates thermal, shot, RTN, and device-mismatch models with device-aware SNR estimation, neural-network co-simulation, NeuroSim circuit modeling, and Bayesian design-technology co-optimization; on 1T FDSOI in-pixel computing it reports 50 fps and 86.8% CIFAR-10 accuracy on an airplane/car/ship three-class subset.
problem: Analog in-pixel computing is energy-efficient for edge AI but device and circuit noise can degrade accuracy, while existing flows lack device-aware cross-layer optimization.
method_or_artifact: Physics-grounded hierarchical noise models, device-aware SNR and neural co-simulation, NeuroSim circuit modeling, and automated Bayesian DTCO exploration.
workload_or_benchmark: Noise-sensitive 1T FDSOI analog in-pixel computing for CIFAR-10 airplane/car/ship three-class classification.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: 1T FDSOI analog in-pixel computing architecture with thermal, shot, RTN, and mismatch sources; array dimensions, voltage, process corner, and NeuroSim configuration are unspecified.
baselines: existing design flows without comprehensive device-aware noise modeling
metrics: 86.8% CIFAR-10 accuracy on a three-class subset
limits: The three-class subset is not full CIFAR-10 and no baseline accuracy, energy, area, or noise-margin comparison is supplied.
Noise distributions, process conditions, ADC/peripheral costs, and Bayesian search budget are unspecified.
Official description only; headline metrics require paper-level verification.

title: CPA-BNN: A Secure and Efficient CIM and PUF Architecture for BNN Accelerator
evidence_span: CPA-BNN uses a 4T2R RRAM cell for in-situ encryption and ciphertext convolution, in-memory batch normalization, PUF entropy extraction, and current-tilt masking; the official description reports approximately 100% key reliability, resistance to model attacks, over 1.4x compute-density improvement, and over 1.6x storage-density improvement over SRAM/NVM BNN schemes.
problem: BNN CIM architectures expose weights in memory cells, leaving models vulnerable to cloning, tampering, and reverse engineering.
method_or_artifact: Secure RRAM CIM with 4T2R in-situ encryption/ciphertext convolution, in-memory batch normalization, intrinsic PUF key extraction, and current-tilt masking.
workload_or_benchmark: Binary neural-network accelerator inference and model-attack resistance; datasets, network sizes, attack suite, and accuracy impact are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: RRAM 4T2R CIM array with integrated PUF and masking; process, voltage, array size, endurance, and peripheral overhead are unspecified.
metrics: Effective prevention of model attacks reported qualitatively
limits: The description does not define the attack model, security game, reliability test population, or accuracy loss.
Density comparisons lack array, peripheral, process, and baseline-normalization conditions.
Official description only; security claims require full-paper and independent review.

title: DAP: A Software/hardware Co-Design for Accelerating Multi-Chip-Based Distributed Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication
evidence_span: DAP combines a two-level matrix partitioning framework with a multi-chip accelerator and an SPU that replaces COO with CSC to reduce communication, limits redundant storage, and uses a reservation buffer for RAW dependencies; simulation reports 1.43x load-balancing improvement, a 0.067x performance penalty from conflicts, and 2.69x geometric-mean throughput relative to an NVIDIA A100 at 500 MHz.
problem: Distributed sparse-dense matrix multiplication suffers workload imbalance, COO metadata traffic, replicated storage pressure, and software preprocessing for floating-point RAW hazards.
method_or_artifact: Two-level partitioning for a 2-D multi-chip array, CSC-based communication-friendly SPU, reduced replication, and reservation-buffer hazard resolution.
workload_or_benchmark: Sparse-dense matrix multiplication for deep learning and scientific computing; sparsity distributions, matrix sizes, chip count, and simulation model are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Multi-chip accelerator array with dedicated SPUs evaluated in simulation at 500 MHz against an NVIDIA A100 reference; interconnect, memory capacity, and area/power conditions are unspecified.
metrics: 0.067x performance penalty attributed to memory-access conflicts
2.69x geometric-mean throughput relative to NVIDIA A100 at 500 MHz
limits: Simulation assumptions, matrix suite, sparsity distributions, chip count, and A100 normalization are not supplied.
The meaning and denominator of the 0.067x penalty require clarification.
Official description only; reported comparisons require paper-level verification.
